meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to arrest', paired with 'арестовать'.

examples.text: Да арестовывать его надо, товарищ генерал!
examples.trans: We just need to arrest him, Comrade General!

examples.text: Ну и процесс остановился. Да арестовывать его надо, товарищ генерал!
examples.trans: And so the process stalled. We just need to arrest him, Comrade General!

meanings.note: a place where old documents are kept

examples.trans: The documents are in the archive.

examples.text: Надоело мне в этом архиве сидеть.
examples.trans: I'm tired of sitting in this archive.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: a high military or security-service rank

examples.trans: Put me through to the general.

examples.text: Генерал Круглов ждёт звонка. Будьте любезны.
examples.trans: General Kruglov is waiting for a call. If you'd be so kind.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement
забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.
The new mayor is Anikeev's deputy.
He's very good with his hands.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: cluster (a big industrial or business project)
meanings.note: in the show: the Moscow investors' project

examples.trans: There will be a cluster in the town.
The mayor is against the cluster.

examples.text: Все в городе хотят этот кластер. Только ты против.
examples.trans: Everyone in town wants this cluster. Only you are against it.

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small, little').
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
He is the mayor of the town.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Всё, давайте. У меня перерыв на обед.
examples.trans: Alright, carry on. I have my lunch break.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.trans: That's what the operation is called.

examples.text: Ты посмотри на этих москвичей, лейтенант. А сами операции проваливают.
examples.trans: Just look at these Moscow types, Lieutenant. And they're the ones who mess up operations.

остановиться.gloss: to stop, to come to a halt

meanings.en: to stop, to pause, to come to a halt

examples.text: Он только начал бояться, а ты остановился!
examples.trans: He just started getting scared, and you stopped!

examples.text: Ваня, ты что? Он только начал бояться, а ты остановился!
examples.trans: Vanya, what is wrong with you? He just started getting scared, and you stopped!

переключиться.gloss: to switch over, to shift focus

examples.text: Заместителю пришлось переключиться на того соседа.
examples.trans: The deputy had to switch his focus to that neighbour.

examples.text: И заместителю пришлось переключиться на того соседа.
examples.trans: And the deputy had to switch his focus to that neighbour.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'путать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to mix up, to confuse', paired with 'путать'.

examples.trans: Yes, go on. Don't mix it up with another one!

examples.text: У меня сейчас перерыв на обед.
examples.trans: I have my lunch break right now.

examples.text: Всё, давайте. У меня перерыв на обед.
examples.trans: Alright, carry on. I have my lunch break.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
Can I go and have a look?
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: impersonal with dative: мне придётся = I'll have to

examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.
We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to continue', paired with 'продолжить'.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'цесс'). Common masculine noun meaning 'process, trial' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ну и процесс остановился. Да арестовывать его надо, товарищ генерал!
examples.trans: And so the process stalled. We just need to arrest him, Comrade General!

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'vial, small bottle, bubble' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That little blue bottle with poison.
A small glass bottle stood on the table.
Did you find the vial? That little blue bottle.

meanings.en: to count on, to rely on
meanings.note: рассчитывать на + accusative: я на тебя рассчитываю = I'm counting on you

examples.text: А без твоих сорока у меня только сто десять. Я на твои деньги рассчитывал.
examples.trans: And without your forty I've only got a hundred and ten. I was counting on your money.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?
Did you find that little blue bottle?
Did you find the vial? That little blue bottle.

meanings.note: в следующий раз = next time; следующий! = next, please!

examples.text: А ты в следующий раз на мои деньги не рассчитывай. И всё будет хорошо.
examples.trans: Well, next time don't count on my money. And everything will be fine.

meanings.note: next door, or in the same flat

examples.text: Соседи, привет! Слушай, дружок, дай свой телефон на минутку.
examples.trans: Hi, neighbours! Listen, buddy, lend me your phone for a minute.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трана'). Common feminine noun meaning 'country' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you!

examples.text: Над тобой вся страна смеётся! Все видели, как ты из окна летел.
examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you! Everyone saw you fly out the window.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

meanings.en: to go on, be happening (usually of chaos or strange events)

examples.trans: So much is going on in the country!

examples.text: А, точно. Перепутал. Такое в стране творится! Продолжаем операцию.
examples.trans: Oh, right. I mixed them up. So much is going on in the country! Continue the operation.

examples.text: Такое в стране творится! Продолжаем операцию.
examples.trans: So much is going on in the country! Continue the operation.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: still the official address in the army and police: 'товарищ генерал'

examples.trans: He's an old friend of mine.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fake, counterfeit, false').

examples.text: У нас фальшивый кластер. Операция «Золотой ярд».
examples.trans: Ours is the fake cluster. Operation Golden Billion.

examples.text: Значит, этот фальшивый мастер украл его.
examples.trans: So that fake repairman stole it.

meanings.en: small bottle, vial (for medicine or perfume)
meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'vial, bottle, flacon' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Did you find the vial? That little blue bottle.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'poison, venom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A little blue bottle with poison.

examples.text: С ядом! А, это же на Урале! Это не у вас.
examples.trans: With poison! Oh, that's in the Urals! That's not your case.
The operation is called Golden Yard.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.
